title: The Fewest Candies That Respect the Ratings

concept.title: Satisfy the left neighbours in one pass, the right neighbours in another, and keep the larger of the two answers
body: Children stand in a line, each with a *rating*. Every child must get **at least one candy**, and a child with a **higher rating than a neighbour** must get **more candies than that neighbour** (children with equal ratings may get any numbers). What is the smallest total number of candies? For the ratings `1 0 2` the answer is 5 (candies `2 1 2`). For `1 2 2` it is 4 (`1 2 1`).

The rule has two parts, one for each side, and each part can be satisfied by a simple pass. **Left to right:** if the child has a higher rating than the child on the left, give one candy more than the left child (otherwise the minimum, 1). This takes care of all the "bigger than my left neighbour" conditions. **Right to left:** if the child has a higher rating than the child on the right and does not have more candies yet, raise it to the right neighbour's candies plus one. Taking the **larger** of the demands from both sides satisfies both rules, and nothing is given beyond what one of the rules requires, so the total is as small as possible.

body.code:
candy = [1] * n
for i in range(1, n):                      # the left neighbour
    if rating[i] > rating[i - 1]:
        candy[i] = candy[i - 1] + 1
for i in range(n - 2, -1, -1):             # the right neighbour
    if rating[i] > rating[i + 1] and candy[i] <= candy[i + 1]:
        candy[i] = candy[i + 1] + 1
print(sum(candy))

body: The second pass may raise a child that the first pass had already set; it never needs to lower anyone, because it only adds when the right neighbour requires more. The total can reach about n^2 / 2 = 1.25 billion for a strictly increasing line, so use 64-bit numbers. Time O(n).

statement: `n` children stand in a line with the given ratings. Each child must get at least one candy, and a child with a higher rating than an adjacent child must get more candies than that child. Print the smallest total number of candies.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of children.
The second line has `n` numbers: the rating of each child, in the order of the line.
outputFormat: Print the smallest total number of candies.
hints: Go from the left: a child with a higher rating than the left neighbour gets one more than that neighbour.
Go from the right: raise a child above the right neighbour if needed. Use 64-bit numbers for the sum.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
rating = list(map(int, input().split()))

explanation: Everyone starts with one candy; a left-to-right pass gives a child one more than the left neighbour when the rating is higher, and a right-to-left pass raises a child above the right neighbour when needed. The sum of the candies is the answer.
